title: Secure SDLC Walkthrough
markdown:
The **Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC)** maps **security activities** to each phase of delivery-**requirements -> design -> implementation -> verification -> release -> operations**-so security is **built in**, not **bolted on** before launch. Product security interviews ask how you integrate **threat modeling**, **secure coding standards**, **SAST/DAST/SCA**, **pen testing**, and **release gates** in **Agile/DevOps** without blocking shipping.

This guide follows the **[Content Mastery Framework](../Interview%20Preparation/Content%20Mastery%20Framework.md)**.

children.title: Phase 4 — Verification & testing
children.markdown:
| Test type | Purpose | Typical placement |
|-----------|---------|-------------------|
| **SAST** | Code patterns, injection sinks | Every PR |
| **SCA** | Known CVEs in deps | Every PR + nightly |
| **Secret scan** | Keys in git | Every PR |
| **DAST** | Running app black-box | Staging nightly / release |
| **IAST** (if used) | Runtime-assisted SAST | Staging |
| **Unit/integration security tests** | AuthZ matrix, IDOR cases | CI |
| **Pen test / bug bounty** | End-to-end validation | Major release / annual |

**Release gate example (Tier 1):** no **Critical/High** open findings without exception; **100%** authZ test pass; threat model **mitigations closed**.

children.title: Misconceptions
"Security is a phase before release."
children.markdown: **Wrong.** Shift-left means **continuous** activities; a single pre-release scan is **too late** for design flaws.
children.notes: Wrong. Shift-left means continuous activities; a single pre-release scan is too late for design flaws.

children.title: "More scanners = more secure."
children.markdown: **Wrong.** Overlapping tools without **dedupe and tuning** creates **noise**, not safety.
children.notes: Wrong. Overlapping tools without dedupe and tuning creates noise, not safety.

children.title: "Threat modeling is only for big projects."
children.markdown: **Wrong.** Small features can introduce **critical** authZ bugs-scope modeling by **risk**, not headcount.
children.notes: Wrong. Small features can introduce critical authZ bugs-scope modeling by risk, not headcount.

children.title: "Developers don't do security."
children.markdown: **Wrong.** AppSec **enables** developers with standards, tools, and champions-they **write** the code.
children.notes: Wrong. AppSec enables developers with standards, tools, and champions-they write the code.

children.title: "Compliance equals secure SDLC."
children.markdown: **Wrong.** SOC 2 checkboxes without **effective gates** still produce vulns.
children.notes: Wrong. SOC 2 checkboxes without effective gates still produce vulns.

children.title: "Pen test replaces SAST/DAST."
children.markdown: **Wrong.** They are **complementary**-automation catches regressions; pen test finds **logic** chains.
children.notes: Wrong. They are complementary-automation catches regressions; pen test finds logic chains.

children.title: Interview prompts
60-second answer
children.markdown:
**Q: How does security fit into the SDLC?**

**A:** Map activities to each phase: **requirements** (data classification, abuse cases), **design** (threat modeling, architecture review), **implementation** (secure coding standards, SCA/SAST in CI), **verification** (DAST, pen test, authZ tests), **release** (config/IAM review, SBOM), and **operations** (vuln mgmt, IR feedback). In Agile, embed these in **Definition of Done** and **risk-tiered gates**-not a waterfall security phase at the end.
children.notes:
Q: How does security fit into the SDLC?

A: Map activities to each phase: requirements (data classification, abuse cases), design (threat modeling, architecture review), implementation (secure coding standards, SCA/SAST in CI), verification (DAST, pen test, authZ tests), release (config/IAM review, SBOM), and operations (vuln mgmt, IR feedback). In Agile, embed these in Definition of Done and risk-tiered gates-not a waterfall security phase at the end.

children.title: When do you threat model?
children.markdown: **A:** New features crossing **trust boundaries**, new **third-party integrations**, **auth changes**, and **multi-tenant** data paths. Update models when architecture shifts-not once per year only.
children.notes: A: New features crossing trust boundaries, new third-party integrations, auth changes, and multi-tenant data paths. Update models when architecture shifts-not once per year only.

children.title: What belongs in CI vs annual pen test?
children.markdown: **A:** **CI:** SCA, secrets, SAST on diff, unit security tests. **Pen test:** business logic, chained exploits, operational config-things automation misses.
children.notes: A: CI: SCA, secrets, SAST on diff, unit security tests. Pen test: business logic, chained exploits, operational config-things automation misses.
children.blurb: A: CI: SCA, secrets, SAST on diff, unit security tests.

children.title: How do you gate releases without blocking all teams?
children.markdown: **A:** **Risk tiers**-Tier 1 internet + PII gets strict gates; Tier 3 internal tools lighter. Async AppSec review with SLAs; **exceptions** with expiry and exec sign-off.
